name: The I.T. Bear Guardian
author: theitbear

sections.description:
The I.T. Bear Guardian slows scrapers and bots that rush through the site. Real customers can still browse, book, and pay. WordPress admin and the login stay open.

This WordPress.org copy uses one mode: Safety Lite. It warns, then blocks, when a visitor hits 12 different pages in 3 minutes.

What you get

  • Safety Lite on pages, posts, and the home page
  • Google and Bing’s own crawlers stay allowed
  • Named bots you can turn off (they start allowed)
  • A block list you can release from, plus an audit log
  • Block emails to an address you set (or the site admin)
  • Optional country name on a block (off until you turn Look up the country on — see External services)
  • No Bear Cave account needed for this copy

Protect Contact

Hide your email, phone, or WhatsApp behind a click-to-reveal control. Paste a shortcode where the plain contact used to sit. Match page, text link, outline, and solid are included. Soft catch can stop more reveals when something acts like a machine.

Bear Guardian (Premium)

Bear Guardian is a separate plugin. This download does not install it. Open Go Premium in the menu to see what it adds, or Upgrade from there.

Premium adds stricter modes (Police State, FBI, Custom), whitelisted addresses, a page group with its own rule, country blocks, named AI crawlers with a host check, timed blocks, and Protect Contact styles (soft, pill, chip, fonts, colours, Alt look, and Hard catch).

External services

The I.T. Bear Guardian can look up the country of a blocked address. That lookup stays off until you tick Look up the country on The I.T. Bear Guardian screen and press Save.

When it is on, and an address is blocked, the plugin sends that address to ipwho.is. ipwho.is is run by ipwhois.io. The reply is the country name, which is shown on the block list and in the block email. No other data is sent. The lookup does not run for an address that is not blocked, and it does not run while the box is unticked.

This service is provided by ipwhois.io: terms of use, privacy policy.
sections.installation:
1. In WordPress, go to Plugins → Add Plugin, search for The I.T. Bear Guardian, and install it. Or upload the zip under Plugins → Add Plugin → Upload Plugin.
  2. Activate the plugin.
  3. Open The I.T. Bear Guardian in the left menu and press Active to turn Safety Lite on.
  4. Optional: set the block email, turn named bots off as you need, and turn on Look up the country only if you want country names on blocks.
  5. Optional: open Protect Contact, add an email, phone, or WhatsApp, choose a look, Save, then paste a shortcode such as [tib_show type="email"] on a page.
  6. To see what Premium adds, open Go Premium. Upgrade opens the Bear Guardian page on The I.T. Bear site. Premium is a separate plugin install, not an in-place upgrade of this one.
sections.changelog:
1.0.3

  • Protect Contact. Click to reveal email, phone, or WhatsApp. Match page, text link, outline, and solid. Soft catch is included.
  • Soft, pill, chip, fonts, colours, Alt look, and Hard catch stay in Bear Guardian Premium. Go Premium describes them and links to Upgrade.
  • Clearer Description and Installation on the WordPress.org listing.

1.0.2

  • Named bots are free. Turning one off refuses a visit that sends that name.
  • Blocked addresses shows Blocks, filters, pages, and a closed audit log.
  • Mail field for block emails. Blank uses the site admin email.
  • Admin notices sit under the header.

1.0.1

  • The readme names this download as The I.T. Bear Guardian. Bear Guardian is a separate plugin.
  • Styles and the Pages script load through WordPress.
  • Country lookup stays off until it is turned on. The readme names ipwho.is.

1.0.0

  • Safety Lite for WordPress.org.
